final_answer.key_evidence_summary: productcatalogservice pod (8458b87d48-7r7l6, worker-01) is the only outlier: 1/2 READY, CrashLoopBackOff, 4 restarts. Doc evidence: server container Last State Terminated Reason=OOMKilled ExitCode=137, memory limit 128Mi, event 'Warning BackOff restarting failed container server'; container dies ~1s after start while logging 'loading catalog from local products.json file...'. Caller side: frontend logs 546x/545x 'rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = no healthy upstream' for /product/{id} and /, and CheckServiceConnectivity(productcatalogservice:3550, its own declared Service port) = Connection Failed. Code face is the break: catalog_loader.go loadCatalogFromLocalFile contains an injected allocation loop appending 8,388,608 ints to a slice on every catalog load (peak ~128MiB, followed by an ineffective runtime.GC()), which collides with the 128Mi limit and OOMKills the process at startup. The resource config matches stock upstream values (limits cpu 200m/memory 128Mi, requests 100m/64Mi), and the same image ran fine on the previous ReplicaSet, so the anomaly resides in the application code, not in the memory configuration or node capacity.
